key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power deepens penetration, higher travel speed narrows and shallows the weld, and higher current widens the weld while stabilizing the arc.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld penetration, geometry, and arc-stability control when manufacturing Invar molds for aerospace composites.
method: Comparison across laser power, travel speed, and welding current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports trends over 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min welding speed, and 150–170 A current, but provides no quantitative validation metrics.
watch_item: Higher power and speed can destabilize the arc; reported trends should not be extrapolated beyond the studied parameter ranges without validation.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
